posts.title: Going all-in with millennial design
posts.excerpt: Solid timber rewards a little patience: it darkens, softens and takes on the marks of everyday life. In this article we look at going all-in with millennial design, what we learned along the way, and the small decisions that make a piece of furniture feel right in a real home.
posts.content:
Solid timber rewards a little patience: it darkens, softens and takes on the marks of everyday life. In this article we look at going all-in with millennial design, what we learned along the way, and the small decisions that make a piece of furniture feel right in a real home.

## Starting with the grain

When we began working on going all-in with millennial design, the brief was simple: make something that is comfortable, honest about its materials and easy to live with. The first sketches were rough, and most of the real decisions happened in the workshop and in customers' homes.

We tried several versions before settling on one we were happy with. Some were too heavy, some too fussy. The one that worked was the one nobody had to explain.

## What we recommend

- Dust with a soft, dry cloth once a week
- Wipe spills straight away and never leave water standing
- Re-oil oak and teak once or twice a year
- Keep pieces out of direct sun and away from radiators

## Bringing it home

Furniture should earn its place. If a piece makes the room calmer, the morning easier or the dinner table longer, it is doing its job. Browse the shop for pieces made with the same care, or get in touch if you would like advice on your own space.
